chapterTitle: Chapter 19 Transition Metals and Coordination Chemistry
title: 19. Check Your Learning

pages.text: Check Your Learning Give an example of an ion from the first transition series with no d electrons.
Check Your Learning Predict what reaction (if any) will occur between HCl and Co(s), and between HBr and Pt(s). You will need to use the standard reduction potentials from Appendix L.
Check Your Learning During the refining of iron, carbon must be present in the blast furnace. Why is carbon necessary to convert iron oxide into iron?
Check Your Learning The complex potassium dicyanoargenate(I) is used to make antiseptic compounds. Give the formula and coordination number.
Check Your Learning Draw the ion trans-diaqua-trans-dibromo-trans-dichlorocobalt(II).

Check Your Learning Some alternative medicine practitioners recommend chelation treatments for ailments that are not clearly related to heavy metals, such as cancer and autism, although the practice is discouraged by many scientific organizations.1 Identify at least two biologically important metals that could be disrupted by chelation therapy.

Check Your Learning The size of the crystal field splitting only influences the arrangement of electrons when there is a choice between pairing electrons and filling the higher-energy orbitals. For which d-electron configurations will there be a difference between high- and low-spin configurations in octahedral complexes?
Check Your Learning Explain how many unpaired electrons a tetrahedral d4 ion will have.
Check Your Learning A complex that appears green, absorbs photons of what wavelengths?
